note: Extension AIX-D1: an audience variant (executive | sop | audit) of ONE generated document. The model writes paragraphs bound to fact ids; the server keeps a paragraph only if every fact id is in the pack, every number and every role word comes from the referenced facts, and the text is plain; a mandatory section without a kept paragraph makes the whole variant a labelled deterministic fallback. Unknowns, limits and the canonical fact table are always rendered by the server. Pinned in docs/evaluation/FINAL_AI_QUALITY_PLAN.md. LHA-D1 (2026-10-18, version 2): every paragraph that cites a rule carries one claim row per cited rule (actor, operator, value, unit, outcome, exceptions stated); the server keeps the paragraph only if each claim equals the canonical fact and the prose agrees with it (comparator next to each threshold, negation, actor bound to the number in the same sentence, contrast terms such as CAPEX/OPEX, currencies, approved/implemented/compliant status words, law or regulation words). Exceptions of the described rules that the kept wording does not state, and facts cut by the pack cap, are disclosed by the server. No model reviewer checks free wording in this version (stated in the limits). Live smoke LHA-SMOKE-20261018-01: the SOP failed the paragraph cap the prompt did not state; the caps are now in the prompt and an SOP may have 12 steps. Second smoke LHA-SMOKE-20261018-02: the model still wrote 18 SOP paragraphs; paragraphs beyond the per-section cap are left out with the reason over_paragraph_cap instead of refusing the whole answer (a section over three times the cap is still refused). Structured-output maxItems was tried and refused by the provider with HTTP 400 (LHA-SMOKE-20261018-03), so the caps are enforced by the server only. Fourth smoke LHA-SMOKE-20261018-04: the SOP guidance asked for steps 'in order' while the prompt forbids inventing an order, and the model answered UNSUPPORTED; the guidance now asks for the checks without an official order. Fifth smoke: a version without any exception made every SOP a fallback; when no offered rule records an exception the server writes the exceptions section itself.

executive.title: Executive summary of the business knowledge

headings.decisions_needed: Decisions people still have to make

executive.guidance: Write for a director who has three minutes: what the rules achieve, where money or control is at risk, what is still undecided. Every material risk must cite the rule or question it comes from.

sop.title: Standard operating procedure derived from the business knowledge
sop.guidance: Write for the person who performs the process: one paragraph per check the performer makes (which condition, which role acts, what happens), grouping related rules when there are many. The facts record no official order: present the checks in a sensible reading order and never call it the required or verified order. Keep every exception of the cited rules in the exceptions section; invent none. Missing process order is not a reason to return UNSUPPORTED.

server_note_when_no_exceptions.exceptions: No exception is recorded for the rules of this knowledge version; every check above applies without an exception in the sources.

audit.title: Audit reading of the business knowledge
audit.guidance: Write for an auditor: one paragraph per control (rule) stating who acts, the threshold or condition, the outcome and whether a person decided it or it is only observed in the sources. Every paragraph cites exactly the rule(s) it describes.
